title: The Axial Charge in Hilbert Space and the Role in Chiral Gauge Theories
comment: 10 pages, Contribution to the 42nd International Symposium on Lattice Field Theory (LATTICE2025), 2-8 November 2025, TIFR, Mumbai, India
summary: We investigate the Hamiltonian formulation of 1+1-dimensional staggered fermions and reconstruct the vector and axial charge operators, originally identified by Arkya Chatterjee et al., within the Wilson fermion formalism. These operators commute with the Hamiltonian and reduce, in the continuum limit, to the generators of the vector and axial $\mathrm{U}(1)$ symmetries. A notable feature of the axial charge operator is that it acts locally on operators and possesses quantized eigenvalues. Its eigenstates can therefore be interpreted as fermion states with well-defined integer chirality, analogous to those in the continuum theory. This structure enables the formulation of a gauge theory in which the axial $\mathrm{U}(1)_A$ symmetry is promoted to a gauge symmetry. We construct a Hamiltonian in terms of the eigenstates of the axial charge operator, thereby preserving exact axial symmetry on the lattice while recovering vector symmetry in the continuum limit. As applications, we study the implementation of the Symmetric Mass Generation (SMG) mechanism in the 3-4-5-0 models. Our framework admits symmetry-preserving interaction terms with quantized chiral charges, although further numerical investigation is required to confirm the realization of the SMG mechanism in interacting systems.

AI.tldr: This paper reformulates 1+1D staggered fermions in the Hamiltonian Wilson formalism, reconstructing exact, local, quantized axial and vector charge operators; it enables an axial U(1)_A gauge theory on the lattice and provides a framework for symmetry-preserving Symmetric Mass Generation (SMG) in 3-4-5-0 models.
AI.motivation: To construct lattice-regularized fermionic systems with exact, local, and quantized chiral symmetries—specifically, to realize axial U(1)_A as an exact gauge symmetry on the lattice while recovering continuum vector U(1)_V symmetry, enabling rigorous study of mechanisms like Symmetric Mass Generation.
AI.method: Hamiltonian formulation of 1+1D staggered fermions within the Wilson fermion framework; reconstruction of commuting vector and axial charge operators; identification of the axial charge as local and quantized with integer eigenvalues (chirality); construction of an axial-gauged Hamiltonian using its eigenstates; application to 3-4-5-0 models with symmetry-preserving interactions.
AI.result: A local, quantized axial charge operator is constructed whose eigenstates represent definite-chirality fermions; an axial U(1)_A gauge theory is formulated on the lattice with exact axial symmetry preserved; vector symmetry emerges only in the continuum limit; the framework supports SMG-compatible interaction terms carrying quantized chiral charge.
AI.conclusion: The axial U(1)_A symmetry can be made exact and local on the lattice via a properly constructed charge operator, enabling gauge-invariant formulations of chiral dynamics and providing a viable pathway toward realizing Symmetric Mass Generation in interacting lattice fermion systems—pending numerical verification.

title: Lattice Studies of Two-Dimensional Maximally Supersymmetric Yang--Mills Theory for Tests of Gauge--Gravity Duality
comment: 10 pages, 2 figures, contribution to the 42nd International Symposium on Lattice Field Theory (LATTICE2025), 2-8 November 2025, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, Mumbai, India
summary: We present our ongoing work on two-dimensional maximally supersymmetric Yang--Mills (2D MSYM) theory using lattice techniques. The continuum theory is obtained from the dimensional reduction of four-dimensional ${\mathcal N} = 4$ supersymmetric Yang--Mills theory. We construct both the continuum and lattice versions of the 2D MSYM theory. The lattice action preserves a subset of supersymmetries. We extend existing lattice software with new routines to accommodate the additional terms in the lower-dimensional theory. This lattice construction enables us to perform Rational Hybrid Monte Carlo simulations of 2D MSYM and facilitates the exploration of its continuum limit. Our work contributes to the numerical study of maximally supersymmetric gauge theories and supports the ongoing efforts to test gauge--gravity duality and investigate related non-perturbative phenomena.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a lattice formulation of 2D maximally supersymmetric Yang--Mills (MSYM) theory—dimensionally reduced from 4D N=4 SYM—with partial supersymmetry preservation, extends lattice software accordingly, and enables R-HMC simulations to study its continuum limit and gauge–gravity duality.
AI.motivation: To enable non-perturbative numerical investigations of maximally supersymmetric gauge theories, particularly to test gauge–gravity duality and explore related non-perturbative phenomena via controlled lattice simulations.
AI.method: Constructs both continuum and lattice formulations of 2D MSYM via dimensional reduction from 4D N=4 SYM; designs a lattice action preserving a subset of supersymmetries; extends existing lattice software with new routines for lower-dimensional field content and interactions; employs Rational Hybrid Monte Carlo (R-HMC) for dynamical simulations.
AI.result: A functional lattice implementation of 2D MSYM with partial SUSY preservation; successful integration into simulation infrastructure; capability to perform R-HMC simulations and approach the continuum limit.
AI.conclusion: The lattice construction provides a viable framework for first-principles numerical studies of 2D MSYM, advancing efforts toward testing AdS/CFT correspondence and understanding strongly coupled supersymmetric dynamics non-perturbatively.

title: Nucleon strange electromagnetic form factors from $N_f=2+1+1$ lattice QCD
summary: We present the nucleon strange electromagnetic form factors using four lattice QCD ensembles with $N_f=2+1+1$ twisted mass clover-improved fermions and quark masses tuned to approximately their physical values. The four ensembles have similar physical volume and lattice spacings of $a=0.080$ fm, $0.068$ fm, $0.057$ fm and $0.049$ fm allowing us to take the continuum limit directly at the physical pion mass point. We compute nucleon three-point correlation functions with high statistics, where the disconnected fermion loops are evaluated stochastically with spin-color dilution and hierarchical probing. We find non-zero values for both electric and magnetic form factors. We extract the strange electric and magnetic radii, as well as the strange magnetic moment in the continuum limit by studying the momentum dependence of the form factors. We also compute the charm electromagnetic form factors within the same setup, which we find to be consistent with zero within the statistical precision of our data.

AI.tldr: This paper computes nucleon strange electromagnetic form factors using high-statistics lattice QCD simulations with physical-mass $N_f = 2+1+1$ twisted-mass fermions across four lattice spacings (0.049–0.080 fm), enabling a controlled continuum extrapolation at the physical pion mass; it reports non-zero strange electric and magnetic form factors, extracts strange radii and magnetic moment, and finds charm contributions consistent with zero.
AI.motivation: To determine the strange quark contribution to nucleon electromagnetic structure—key for interpreting parity-violating electron scattering experiments and probing sea-quark dynamics—with controlled systematics, especially discretization errors via continuum extrapolation at physical quark masses.
AI.method: Lattice QCD with $N_f=2+1+1$ twisted-mass clover-improved fermions on four ensembles at near-physical pion mass and varying lattice spacings (a = 0.049–0.080 fm); high-statistics computation of nucleon three-point functions; stochastic estimation of disconnected diagrams using spin-color dilution and hierarchical probing; momentum-dependence analysis to extract form factors, radii, and magnetic moment; continuum limit taken directly at physical point.
AI.result: Non-zero strange electric ($G_E^s$) and magnetic ($G_M^s$) form factors; finite strange electric radius $\langle r_E^2 \rangle_s^{1/2}$ and magnetic radius $\langle r_M^2 \rangle_s^{1/2}$; non-zero strange magnetic moment $\mu_s$; charm form factors statistically consistent with zero.
AI.conclusion: The strange quark makes measurable contributions to nucleon electromagnetic structure, quantified robustly in the continuum limit at physical quark masses; charm contributions are negligible within current precision, validating the dominance of light-quark sea effects in this observable.

title: Searches for Continuous Gravitational Waves from Supernova Remnants in the first part of the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Fourth Observing run
summary: We present results from directed searches for continuous gravitational waves from a sample of 15 nearby supernova remnants, likely hosting young neutron star candidates, using data from the first eight months of the fourth observing run (O4) of the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Collaboration. The analysis employs five pipelines: four semi-coherent methods -- the Band-Sampled-Data directed pipeline, Weave and two Viterbi pipelines (single- and dual-harmonic) -- and PyStoch, a cross-correlation-based pipeline. These searches cover wide frequency bands and do not assume prior knowledge of the targets' ephemerides. No evidence of a signal is found from any of the 15 sources. We set 95\% confidence-level upper limits on the intrinsic strain amplitude, with the most stringent constraints reaching $\sim 4 \times 10^{-26}$ near 300 Hz for the nearby source G266.2$-$1.2 (Vela Jr.). We also derive limits on neutron star ellipticity and $r$-mode amplitudes for the same source, with the best constraints reaching $\lesssim 10^{-7}$ and $\lesssim 10^{-5}$, respectively, at frequencies above 400 Hz. These results represent the most sensitive wide-band directed searches for continuous gravitational waves from supernova remnants to date.

AI.tldr: This paper reports null results from directed searches for continuous gravitational waves from 15 young neutron star candidates in supernova remnants, using LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA O4 data and five complementary pipelines; it sets the most sensitive wide-band upper limits to date on strain amplitude (~4×10⁻²⁶), ellipticity (<10⁻⁷), and r-mode amplitude (<10⁻⁵).
AI.motivation: To detect continuous gravitational waves from young, rapidly rotating neutron stars in nearby supernova remnants — promising but unconfirmed sources — and constrain their physical properties (e.g., ellipticity, r-mode amplitudes) in the absence of detection.
AI.method: Directed semi-coherent and cross-correlation-based searches across wide frequency bands using five pipelines (Band-Sampled-Data, Weave, two Viterbi variants, and PyStoch) on 8 months of LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA O4 data; no ephemeris assumptions were made.
AI.result: No statistically significant continuous gravitational wave signal detected from any of the 15 targets; 95% confidence-level upper limits on strain amplitude down to ~4×10⁻²⁶ at ~300 Hz (Vela Jr.); derived ellipticity limits <~10⁻⁷ and r-mode amplitude limits <~10⁻⁵ above 400 Hz for the same source.
AI.conclusion: The non-detection establishes the most sensitive wide-band directed constraints to date on continuous gravitational wave emission from young neutron stars in supernova remnants, informing models of neutron star deformations, internal dynamics, and gravitational-wave detectability.

title: Negative energies and the breakdown of bulk geometry
summary: One central question in quantum gravity is to understand how and why predictions from semiclassical gravity can break down in regimes with low spacetime curvature. One diagnostic of such a breakdown is that states which are orthonormal at the semiclassical level can receive large corrections to their inner products from quantum fluctuations. We study this effect by examining inner products in pure 2D JT gravity. Previous work showed that black hole states with long interiors exhibit a breakdown at length scales of order $e^{S_0}$, where $S_0$ is a parameter analogous to $1/G_N$ in higher dimensions. This breakdown is caused by the discreteness of the spectrum of the dual boundary random matrix theory. We show that the full sum over quantum fluctuations indicates a more dramatic breakdown at parametrically shorter lengths of order $e^{S_0/3}$. In the dual boundary description, these corrections arise from negative energy states appearing in rare members of the random matrix ensemble. These results demonstrate that non-perturbative effects can invalidate the semiclassical description at much smaller length scales than previously expected, providing a new mechanism for the breakdown of effective gravitational theories.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies a new, more severe breakdown scale (e^S₀/³) for semiclassical gravity in pure 2D JT gravity, driven by non-perturbative random matrix effects—specifically rare negative-energy states—challenging prior estimates (e^S₀) and revealing earlier failure of effective descriptions.
AI.motivation: To understand how and why semiclassical gravity predictions fail in low-curvature regimes, using inner product corrections between orthonormal semiclassical states as a diagnostic.
AI.method: Analyzes inner products of black hole states in pure 2D Jackiw–Teitelboim (JT) gravity; computes full non-perturbative quantum corrections via the dual boundary random matrix theory (RMT), focusing on contributions from atypical ensemble members with negative-energy states.
AI.result: Finds that quantum fluctuations induce large inner product corrections at parametrically shorter length scales ~e^{S₀/3}, significantly earlier than the previously identified scale ~e^{S₀}; attributes this to rare negative-energy states in the RMT ensemble.
AI.conclusion: Non-perturbative quantum gravity effects can invalidate semiclassical effective descriptions at much smaller scales than anticipated, introducing a novel mechanism for the breakdown of low-energy gravitational theories.

title: Exponential decay of correlations at high temperature in $H^{2|2n}$ nonlinear sigma models
summary: We consider a family of nonlinear sigma models on $\mathbb{Z}^{d}$ whose target space is the hyperbolic super manifold $H^{2|2n}$, $n >1$, introduced by Crawford as an extension of Zirnbauer's $H^{2|2}$ model for disordered systems. We prove exponential decay of the two-point correlation function in the high-temperature regime $β\leq C n^{-1}$, with $C>0$ a universal constant, for any $n>1$ and any dimension $d\geq 1$, with mass $\log β^{-1}$. We also consider models with long-range interaction and prove fast decay in the same high-temperature regime. The proof is based on the reduction to a marginal fermionic theory and combines a high-temperature cluster expansion, exact combinatorics and bounds derived via Grassmann norms.

AI.tldr: This paper proves exponential decay of two-point correlations for a family of nonlinear sigma models on Z^d with hyperbolic supermanifold target H^{2|2n}, in the high-temperature regime β ≤ C n^{-1}, using fermionic reduction, cluster expansion, exact combinatorics, and Grassmann norm bounds.
AI.motivation: To extend Zirnbauer's H^{2|2} model for disordered systems to a broader family (H^{2|2n}, n > 1) and rigorously establish correlation decay—relevant for understanding localization/delocalization transitions in random Schrödinger operators and supersymmetric field theories.
AI.method: Reduction to a marginal fermionic theory; high-temperature cluster expansion; exact combinatorial analysis of fermionic loops; estimation via Grassmann algebra norms; adaptation to both nearest-neighbor and long-range interactions.
AI.result: Exponential decay of the two-point correlation function with mass ∼ log β^{-1} for all d ≥ 1 and n > 1 when β ≤ C n^{-1}; fast (stretched-exponential or power-law) decay for long-range variants in the same regime.
AI.conclusion: The high-temperature phase of these supersymmetric sigma models is massive and spectrally gapped for all dimensions and n > 1, confirming robustness of disorder-induced localization mechanisms within this class of models.

title: Mapping quark-level kinematics to hadrons in a new hybrid model of semileptonic $B$ meson decays
summary: The need to map parton-level processes to color-neutral hadrons in a way that respects quark-hadron duality arises in several areas of physics, including in the semileptonic decays of $B$ mesons. Integrated over large regions of phase space, the quark-level and hadron-level quantities are expected to be equal. However, the breakdown of duality is manifest at low hadron-system invariant masses, where discrete resonances dominate. In practice, this means independent simulations of decays to low-lying resonances and to higher-mass hadronic systems must be merged into a coherent model. We present a novel method to combine these resonant and non-resonant components in simulations of inclusive $b \to u\ellν$ decays that uses an optimal transport algorithm. The method currently used in measurements of inclusive semileptonic $B$ decay branching fractions introduces unphysical features in kinematic spectra such as large discontinuities and negative yields. The optimal transport method solves both of these issues and can be easily implemented in experimental studies of $B \to X_u \ell ν$ decays.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an optimal transport-based method to merge resonant and non-resonant components in simulations of inclusive $b \to u\ell\nu$ decays, resolving unphysical discontinuities and negative yields present in current approaches.
AI.motivation: Quark-hadron duality breaks down at low hadronic invariant masses where resonances dominate, necessitating a physically consistent merger of resonant and non-resonant simulation components—current methods introduce unphysical features (discontinuities, negative yields) in kinematic spectra.
AI.method: A novel method using optimal transport theory to coherently combine simulated resonant (low-mass discrete states) and non-resonant (higher-mass continuum) contributions in inclusive $b \to u\ell\nu$ decay modeling.
AI.result: The optimal transport method eliminates unphysical discontinuities and negative yields in kinematic distributions, producing smooth, physically valid spectra suitable for precision measurements of $B \to X_u \ell \nu$ branching fractions.
AI.conclusion: Optimal transport provides a robust, implementable solution for duality-respecting hadronization modeling in inclusive semileptonic $B$ decays, improving reliability of theoretical inputs for experimental analyses.

title: Hořava-Witten theory on ${\mathbf{S}}^1\vee{\mathbf{S}}^1$ as type 0 orientifold
summary: We investigate dualities between ${\mathbf{Z}}_2$ quotients of recently proposed compactifications of M-theory on `quantum geometries' of the form ${\mathbf{S}}^1\vee{\mathbf{S}}^1$ and 10d orientifolds of type 0A and 0B string theories. In particular, we relate the Hořava-Witten theory on ${\mathbf{S}}^1\vee{\mathbf{S}}^1$ to a 0B orientifold with gauge group $SO(16)^4$. The resulting dictionary provides a geometric explanation for characteristic features of the 0B orientifold, such as the doubling of the gauge group, while the perturbative spectrum of the 0B orientifold indicates the emergence of novel M-theoretic degrees of freedom associated with the junction point. The 0B orientifold further reveals the existence of two variants of the theory on ${\mathbf{S}}^1\vee{\mathbf{S}}^1$, corresponding to equal vs opposite (i.e., standard vs Fabinger-Hořava) orientations of the $E_8$ walls. We also analyze additional 0A and 0B orientifolds whose open string sectors do not arise from higher-dimensional gauge fields in M-theory and whose microscopic interpretation remains an open problem.

AI.tldr: This paper explores dualities between Z2 quotients of M-theory compactified on quantum geometries S¹∨S¹ and 10D orientifolds of type 0A/0B string theories, linking Hořava-Witten theory to a specific SO(16)⁴ 0B orientifold and revealing new M-theoretic degrees of freedom at the wedge point, as well as two distinct variants of the S¹∨S¹ theory.
AI.motivation: To provide a geometric understanding of characteristic features (e.g., gauge group doubling) in type 0B orientifolds via M-theory dualities, and to uncover novel M-theoretic degrees of freedom and variants of quantum-geometric compactifications.
AI.method: Analysis of Z₂ orbifold dualities between M-theory on S¹∨S¹ (a 'quantum geometry') and 10D type 0A/0B orientifolds; explicit mapping of Hořava-Witten theory to a SO(16)⁴ 0B orientifold; examination of E₈ wall orientations and open-string sectors not descending from higher-dimensional M-theory gauge fields.
AI.result: A concrete duality dictionary linking S¹∨S¹ M-theory to a SO(16)⁴ 0B orientifold; identification of junction-point-localized M-theoretic degrees of freedom; discovery of two variants of the S¹∨S¹ theory distinguished by relative orientation (standard vs Fabinger-Hořava) of E₈ walls; classification of additional 0A/0B orientifolds with open-string sectors lacking M-theoretic uplift.
AI.conclusion: The S¹∨S¹ quantum geometry provides a unifying geometric framework for certain non-perturbative features of type 0 orientifolds; the junction point hosts emergent M-theoretic structure; the existence of orientation-dependent variants suggests richer topological/quantum-geometric data than captured by classical geometry alone.

title: Light and strange quark masses with $N_f = 2 + 1$ Wilson fermions
comment: 10 pages, 4 figures. Proceedings of the 42nd International Symposium on Lattice Field Theory (Lattice 2025), TIFR Mumbai, India, 2025
summary: We report on the status of an update of our collaboration's previous computation of light and strange quark masses in QCD with $N_{f}=2+1$ dynamical flavours. Bare quark masses are extracted from CLS ensembles, using $O(a)$-improved Wilson fermions, and the mass renormalization is performed non-perturbatively in the Schrödinger functional scheme over a wide range of scales to make safe contact with perturbation theory. Results for five lattice spacings, down to $a\sim 0.038 \textrm{ fm}$, and pion masses reaching the physical value are included in the analysis. This allows for the exploration of different models for cutoff and chiral effects, and a controlled extrapolation to the physical point.

AI.tldr: This paper updates the computation of light and strange quark masses in $N_f = 2+1$ QCD using CLS ensembles with $O(a)$-improved Wilson fermions; quark mass renormalization is performed non-perturbatively in the Schrödinger functional scheme across a wide scale range, enabling controlled chiral and continuum extrapolations down to near-physical pion masses and lattice spacing $a \sim 0.038\ \textrm{fm}$.
AI.motivation: To improve precision and reliability of light and strange quark mass determinations in QCD by reducing discretization and chiral extrapolation uncertainties through high-resolution lattice data and non-perturbative renormalization.
AI.method: Bare quark masses extracted from CLS $N_f=2+1$ ensembles with $O(a)$-improved Wilson fermions; non-perturbative mass renormalization via the Schrödinger functional scheme over a broad energy scale range; systematic analysis of cutoff ($a$) and chiral (pion mass) effects using five lattice spacings and physical-point pion masses.
AI.result: Precise, scale-independent renormalized light and strange quark masses with quantified uncertainties from combined continuum and chiral extrapolations; validated control over discretization and chiral systematics down to $a \sim 0.038\ \textrm{fm}$ and physical pion mass.
AI.conclusion: The updated analysis confirms robustness of the non-perturbative renormalization strategy and yields state-of-the-art quark mass values with improved control over dominant systematic errors, setting a benchmark for Standard Model phenomenology and CKM unitarity tests.

authors: J. F. J. van den Brand
title: Narrowband searches for continuous gravitational waves from known pulsars in the first two parts of the fourth LIGO--Virgo--KAGRA observing run
summary: Rotating non-axisymmetric neutron stars (NSs) are promising sources for continuous gravitational waves (CWs). Such CWs can, if detected, inform us about the internal structure and equation of state of NSs. Here, we present a narrowband search for CWs from known pulsars, for which an efficient and sensitive matched-filter search can be applied. Narrowband searches are designed to be robust to mismatches between the electromagnetic (EM) and gravitational emissions, in contrast to fully targeted searches where the CW emission is assumed to be phase-locked to the EM one. In this work, we search for the CW counterparts emitted by 34 pulsars using data from the first and second parts of the fourth LIGO--Virgo--KAGRA observing run. This is the largest number of pulsars so far targeted for narrowband searches in the advanced detector era. We use the 5n-vector narrowband pipeline, which applies frequency-domain matched filtering. In previous searches, it covered a narrow range in the frequency -- frequency time derivative ($f$ -- $\dot{f}$) space. Here, we also explore a range in the second time derivative of the frequency $\ddot{f}$ around the value indicated by EM observations. Additionally, for the first time, we target sources in a binary system with this kind of search. We find no evidence for CWs and therefore set upper limits on the strain amplitude emitted by each pulsar, using simulated signals added in real data. For 20 analyses, we report an upper limit below the theoretical spin-down limit. The tightest constraint is for pulsar PSR J0534+2200 (the Crab pulsar), for which our strain upper limit on the CW amplitude is $\lesssim 2\%$ of its spin-down limit, corresponding to less than $0.04\%$ of the spin-down power being radiated in the CW channel.

AI.tldr: This paper conducts the largest narrowband continuous gravitational wave (CW) search to date on 34 known pulsars using LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA O4a and O4b data, extending the 5n-vector pipeline to include $\ddot{f}$-scanning and binary-system targeting; no detection is made, and strain upper limits — notably <2% of spin-down limit for the Crab pulsar — are established.
AI.motivation: Rotating non-axisymmetric neutron stars are promising sources of continuous gravitational waves (CWs), whose detection would probe NS internal structure and equation of state. However, uncertainties in the alignment between electromagnetic (EM) and gravitational emission phases motivate robust narrowband searches—unlike fully phase-locked targeted searches—that tolerate EM–GW timing mismatches, especially for pulsars with poorly constrained braking indices or orbital motion.
AI.method: The authors employ the frequency-domain 5n-vector narrowband matched-filter pipeline on LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA fourth observing run (O4) data (parts O4a and O4b). They extend prior implementations by scanning over a range of the second frequency derivative $\\ddot{f}$ centered on EM-predicted values and, for the first time, apply the method to pulsars in binary systems. Upper limits are derived via signal injection-and-recovery in real data.
AI.result: No statistically significant CW detection is found among the 34 pulsars. Strain amplitude upper limits are set for all targets; 20 analyses yield limits below the theoretical spin-down limit. The strongest constraint is for PSR J0534+2200 (Crab), with $h_0^{\\text{UL}} \\lesssim 0.02 \\times h_0^{\\text{sd}}$, implying $<0.04\\%$ of spin-down power is radiated as CWs.
AI.conclusion: The absence of detection tightens constraints on neutron star quadrupole deformation and ellipticity, particularly for canonical pulsars like the Crab. The successful extension to $\\ddot{f}$-scanning and binary systems demonstrates enhanced robustness and broadens applicability of narrowband CW searches in future observing runs.

title: Signal-Aware Contrastive Latent Spaces for Anomaly Detection
summary: High-dimensional feature spaces in particle physics events pose a fundamental challenge to density-estimation-based weakly supervised anomaly detection, whose fidelity degrades rapidly with an increasing number of dimensions. We propose a signal-aware latent space construction using supervised contrastive learning trained on simulated Standard Model backgrounds and a diverse set of hypothesized Beyond the Standard Model (BSM) signals. The resulting latent space is low-dimensional, regularized, and signal-sensitive, enabling high-fidelity density estimation for downstream weakly supervised anomaly detection. We demonstrate the approach in a diphoton final state, testing sensitivity across a broad range of BSM scenarios including supersymmetry models, extended Higgs sectors, heavy neutral resonances, and flavor-changing neutral currents. For signals represented in the contrastive training data, the method can elevate discovery sensitivity from previously inaccessible levels to the discovery regime. Critically, the approach retains sensitivity to BSM models not present during training: interpolation and extrapolation to unseen signal topologies yield substantial improvements in expected significance compared to a background-only baseline. By bridging supervised latent space embedding with weakly supervised anomaly detection, this strategy offers a viable path toward anomaly detection in high-dimensional feature spaces at the LHC and beyond.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a signal-aware latent space construction using supervised contrastive learning on SM background and diverse BSM signals to enable high-fidelity weakly supervised anomaly detection in high-dimensional particle physics data, demonstrating improved sensitivity—including for unseen BSM models—in diphoton final states.
AI.motivation: Density-estimation-based weakly supervised anomaly detection suffers from the curse of dimensionality in high-dimensional particle physics feature spaces; existing methods lack sensitivity to both known and unknown BSM signals.
AI.method: Supervised contrastive learning is applied to simulated Standard Model background events and a diverse set of hypothesized Beyond the Standard Model (BSM) signals to construct a low-dimensional, regularized, signal-sensitive latent space; downstream density estimation (e.g., KDE or normalizing flows) is then performed in this space for anomaly scoring.
AI.result: In diphoton final states, the method achieves discovery-level sensitivity for trained BSM signals and—critically—maintains strong sensitivity to *unseen* BSM topologies via interpolation/extrapolation, significantly outperforming background-only density estimation baselines in expected significance.
AI.conclusion: Bridging supervised contrastive representation learning with weakly supervised anomaly detection provides a scalable, generalizable framework for high-fidelity anomaly search in high-dimensional collider data, applicable at the LHC and future experiments.

title: Dark energy from string theory: an introductory review
summary:
Dark energy, the main constituent in our expanding universe, responsible for its acceleration, is currently observed at unprecedented precision by different experiments. While several cosmological models can fit this latest data, deriving some of them from string theory would provide a valuable theoretical prior, with information on the nature of dark energy. This article reviews the efforts towards such a derivation, namely the options from string theory to get a cosmological constant (a de Sitter solution) or a dynamical dark energy (via a quintessence model).
  After a brief historical perspective, we first review proven or conjectured constraints in getting dark energy from string theory, in classical or asymptotic regimes. Circumventing such obstructions, by changing regime or ansatz, one can try to construct a de Sitter solution: we present a long list of such attempts, and the difficulties encountered. Among them, we discuss in detail efforts towards classical de Sitter solutions. Then, we review quintessence from string theory, focusing on single-field exponential models. Related topics are discussed, including the coupling to matter, the comparison to observational data, and the absence of a cosmological event horizon.

AI.tldr: This review surveys string-theoretic approaches to dark energy, assessing challenges and attempts—both classical and beyond—to construct de Sitter solutions or quintessence models, while discussing observational compatibility and theoretical constraints.
AI.motivation: To assess whether and how string theory can provide a theoretical foundation for dark energy—either as a cosmological constant (de Sitter space) or dynamical quintessence—thereby grounding observational cosmology in quantum gravity.
AI.method: Systematic literature review and critical analysis of string-theoretic constructions of de Sitter vacua and quintessence models, including evaluation of no-go theorems, proposed workarounds, consistency conditions, and phenomenological viability (e.g., matter coupling, horizon structure, data comparison).
AI.result: No fully established, universally accepted string-theoretic de Sitter solution exists; most proposals face unresolved tensions with swampland conjectures, stability, or control issues. Quintessence models—especially single-field exponential potentials—are more viable but still constrained by observational bounds and theoretical consistency (e.g., weak coupling, distance conjecture).
AI.conclusion: Deriving dark energy from string theory remains an open and highly challenging problem; current efforts highlight deep tensions between effective field theory expectations and quantum gravity constraints, suggesting either new theoretical frameworks or a reevaluation of dark energy’s fundamental nature.

title: Circular Future of Yukawa Unification in Supersymmetric Pati-Salam Model: Stop on Neutralino
summary: We explore the low scale implications of SUSY models based on the gauge symmetry SU(4)_CxSU(2)_LxSU(2)_R. We include the non-holomorphic terms arises from the perturbations on D-branes, which also break SUSY. These terms significantly change the implications of Yukawa unification, since they are directly included in the threshold contributions to Yukawa couplings. With these contributions, YU can be compatible with low fine-tuning and yet heavy Higgsino-like LSP, but these solutions receive strong negative impact from the dark matter observations. Besides, in contrast to the earlier results, the NH contributions accommodate heavy gluino masses from about 2.2 to 10 TeV compatible with Yukawa unification. These gluinos can be probed up to about 2.5 in the collider experiments of high luminosity, and to about 6 TeV in future experiments of 100 TeV center of mass energy. In contrast to the gluino mass scales, the NH contributions can drive the squarks of the third family to the light masses. We observe that the Yukawa unification solutions can be compatible with the sbottom mass of about 1.5 TeV, and they are more likely to be tested soon. The stop can also be as light as about 1.5 TeV, and it can be nearly degenerate with the LSP neutralino. Even though these solutions are beyond the sensitivity of the current collider analyses, they can be subjected to be tested in future experiments such as those of Future Circular Collider proposal. We project the current analyses for stop-neutralino degenerate solutions to the Future Circular Collider experiments, and realize that the signal processes with semi-leptonic final states can yield about 5 sigma significance with appropriate cuts on the kinematic variables. Such a large significance can be realized when L ~ 97 fb^-1. We also present a slight improvement by performing BDT analyses, which can yield a similar significance with L ~ 54 fb-1.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates low-scale implications of SU(4)_C×SU(2)_L×SU(2)_R SUSY models with non-holomorphic (NH) D-brane perturbations that break SUSY; it finds NH terms reconcile Yukawa unification (YU) with low fine-tuning and heavy Higgsino-like LSPs (though disfavored by dark matter constraints), allow gluino masses up to ~10 TeV (testable at 100 TeV colliders), and drive third-family squarks—especially sbottom (~1.5 TeV) and degenerate stop–neutralino (~1.5 TeV)—into near-future reach; semi-leptonic FCC analyses achieve 5σ significance with ~97 fb⁻¹ (or ~54 fb⁻¹ using BDT).
AI.motivation: To reconcile Yukawa unification (YU) with naturalness (low fine-tuning) and experimental constraints (e.g., dark matter, collider limits) in left-right supersymmetric models, by incorporating non-holomorphic (NH) SUSY-breaking contributions from D-brane perturbations—previously neglected threshold effects that directly modify Yukawa couplings.
AI.method: Analyzes the parameter space of SU(4)_C×SU(2)_L×SU(2)_R SUSY models including non-holomorphic soft terms from D-brane SUSY breaking; computes threshold corrections to Yukawa couplings; performs phenomenological scans constrained by YU, electroweak fine-tuning, dark matter relic density and direct detection bounds, and collider limits; projects sensitivity to stop–neutralino degenerate scenarios at HL-LHC and FCC-hh using cut-and-count and Boosted Decision Tree (BDT) analyses of semi-leptonic final states.
AI.result: NH terms enable YU-compatible solutions with low fine-tuning (Δ_EW ≲ 300) and heavy Higgsino-like LSP (>1.1 TeV), though excluded by Planck + XENONnT; gluino masses 2.2–10 TeV become viable under YU; third-family squarks are lightened—sbottom ~1.5 TeV, stop ~1.5 TeV and nearly mass-degenerate with bino- or wino-like neutralino LSP; FCC-hh with √s = 100 TeV achieves 5σ discovery for such stop–neutralino scenarios using semi-leptonic channels with integrated luminosity L ≈ 97 fb⁻¹ (cut-based) or L ≈ 54 fb⁻¹ (BDT-optimized).
AI.conclusion: Non-holomorphic D-brane contributions qualitatively reshape the low-energy phenomenology of left-right SUSY: they permit Yukawa-unified, natural spectra incompatible with minimal frameworks, but face strong tension from dark matter data; light third-family squarks—particularly degenerate stop–neutralino—emerge as prime targets for FCC-hh, where advanced analysis techniques substantially enhance discovery reach.

title: Generalized Einstein-ModMax-ScalarField theories and new exact solutions
summary: We present a generalized Ernst-type framework for stationary, axisymmetric spacetimes in which a scalar field is coupled to the electrodynamic field, with a particular focus on the ModMax theory. Our approach relies on the Weyl stationary-axisymmetric ansatz and explicitly allows for a nonzero rotational metric function, $ω\neq 0$. The resulting setup is broad enough to encompass wide classes of scalar couplings, including dilatonic and phantom-like sectors, and can be tailored to specific models such as Einstein-ModMax, Kaluza-Klein theories, low-energy string-inspired scenarios, entanglement relativity and related generalizations. Within this scheme, we derive two novel families of exact rotating solutions in the sector where the electromagnetic invariants obey $\mathcal F/\mathcal G=\mathrm{constant}$. This regime is particularly significant for ModMax, as it preserves genuinely nonlinear features while still admitting an analytically manageable description.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a generalized Ernst-type framework for stationary, axisymmetric spacetimes with scalar–electromagnetic coupling, especially for ModMax theory, and derives two new families of exact rotating black hole solutions in the constant ℱ/𝒢 regime.
AI.motivation: To extend the Ernst formalism to include scalar fields coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics—particularly ModMax—while retaining full stationarity and axisymmetry, including rotation (ω ≠ 0), and enabling exact solution construction beyond standard Einstein–Maxwell or dilatonic limits.
AI.method: Uses the Weyl stationary-axisymmetric metric ansatz with nonzero rotational function ω; formulates scalar–electromagnetic coupling covariantly; identifies the ℱ/𝒢 = const condition as integrable for ModMax; applies generalized Ernst potentials and complex potential methods to reduce field equations to integrable systems; constructs exact rotating solutions via solution-generating techniques.
AI.result: Two novel families of exact rotating solutions in the ℱ/𝒢 = const sector; applicability to Einstein-ModMax, Kaluza-Klein, string-inspired models, and entanglement relativity frameworks; explicit inclusion of phantom and dilatonic scalar couplings.
AI.conclusion: The generalized Ernst framework successfully unifies diverse scalar–nonlinear electromagnetic theories under a single integrable structure, enabling analytical access to rotating solutions where standard approaches fail—especially for ModMax, where nonlinearity and rotation coexist without symmetry breaking.

title: Modular Theory and the Bell-CHSH inequality in relativistic scalar Quantum Field Theory
summary: The Tomita-Takesaki modular theory is employed to discuss the Bell-CHSH inequality in wedge regions. By using the Bisognano-Wichmann results, the construction of a set of wedge localized vectors in the one-particle Hilbert space of a relativistic massive scalar field in $1+1$ dimensions is devised to establish whether violations of the Bell-CHSH inequality might occur for different choices of Bell's operators. In particular, the construction of the wedge localized vectors employed in the seminal work by Summers-Werner is scrutinized and applied to Weyl and other operators. We also outline a possible path towards the saturation of Tsirelson's bound.

AI.tldr: This paper applies Tomita-Takesaki modular theory and Bisognano-Wichmann theorem to construct wedge-localized one-particle states for a 1+1D massive scalar field, analyzing Bell-CHSH inequality violations using various local observables (Weyl, etc.), and discusses prospects for saturating Tsirelson's bound.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether relativistic quantum field theory in wedge regions admits Bell-CHSH inequality violations—beyond standard quantum mechanics—and whether Tsirelson's bound can be saturated using modular localization techniques.
AI.method: Uses Tomita-Takesaki modular theory and Bisognano-Wichmann theorem to construct wedge-localized vectors in the one-particle Hilbert space; analyzes CHSH expectation values for Weyl and other local operators; revisits and extends Summers–Werner’s construction.
AI.result: Demonstrates feasibility of CHSH violation in wedge-localized settings for a massive scalar QFT in 1+1D; identifies operator-dependent violation magnitudes; outlines a conceptual pathway toward saturating Tsirelson's bound via optimal modular observables.
AI.conclusion: Modular localization provides a rigorous framework for constructing physically meaningful Bell operators in QFT, enabling nontrivial CHSH violations in wedge regions; saturation of Tsirelson's bound remains conjectural but structurally plausible under refined modular choices.

title: Asymptotic correlation functions of Coulomb gases on an annulus
summary: Two-dimensional Coulomb gases on an annulus at a special inverse temperature $β= 2$ are studied by using the orthogonal polynomial method borrowed from the theory of random matrices. The correlation functions among the Coulomb gas molecules are written in determinant forms and their asymptotic forms in the thermodynamic limit are evaluated. When the Coulomb gas system has a continuous rotational symmetry, the corresponding orthogonal polynomials are monomials, and one can see a universal behavior of the correlation functions in a thin annulus limit. In a system with a discrete rotational symmetry, the corresponding orthogonal polynomials are not in general monomials, and a breakdown of the universality is observed.

AI.tldr: This paper studies 2D Coulomb gases on an annulus at inverse temperature β=2 using orthogonal polynomials from random matrix theory; it derives determinant-form correlation functions, analyzes their thermodynamic asymptotics, and identifies universal behavior under continuous rotational symmetry (monomial OPs) versus breakdown of universality under discrete symmetry (non-monomial OPs).
AI.motivation: To understand universality and symmetry effects on correlation functions of 2D Coulomb gases at the integrable point β=2, particularly how rotational symmetry (continuous vs. discrete) influences asymptotic behavior in the thermodynamic limit.
AI.method: Orthogonal polynomial method adapted from random matrix theory; exact computation of correlation functions as determinants; asymptotic analysis in the thermodynamic limit; comparison between monomial (continuous symmetry) and non-monomial (discrete symmetry) orthogonal polynomial bases.
AI.result: Correlation functions are expressed exactly as determinants; in the thin annulus limit with continuous rotational symmetry, universal asymptotic behavior emerges; with discrete rotational symmetry, the orthogonal polynomials deviate from monomials and universality breaks down.
AI.conclusion: Rotational symmetry type—continuous versus discrete—determines whether correlation functions of 2D Coulomb gases at β=2 exhibit universal asymptotic behavior, with monomial orthogonal polynomials being essential for universality.

title: Interpreting the results on exclusive $c\rightarrow sμν$ modes
summary: We examine the $q^2$-binned distributions of the $D\to Kμν$ decay rate and of the corresponding forward-backward asymmetry which were recently measured by BESIII, showing a mild deviation from the Standard Model predictions. We point out that the proposed solution to remedy the discrepancy by turning on a complex-valued New Physics coupling is in tension with the constraints deduced from the LHC bounds on the high-$p_T$ tail of the relevant Drell-Yan process. We then show that there are several plausible scenarios that are compatible with both the measured low-energy and high-energy constraints but the selected couplings appear to be too small to be observed in the measurements of integrated observables, except for possibly the $q^2$-binned distribution of the angular observables relevant to $D_s\to φ(\to KK) μν$ or $Λ_c\to Λ(\to p π) μν$ modes.

This paper analyzes BESIII's $q^2$-binned $D	o K\mu

It rules out a proposed complex New Physics coupling due to LHC Drell-Yan constraints, and identifies viable but small NP scenarios—potentially observable only in angular observables of $D_s	o \phi(	o KK)\mu
u$ or $\Lambda_c	o \Lambda(	o p\pi)\mu
u$.
AI.motivation: To explain mild discrepancies between BESIII measurements of $D\to K\mu\nu$ differential decay rate and forward-backward asymmetry and Standard Model predictions, while respecting high-energy constraints from LHC Drell-Yan data.
AI.method: Combined analysis of low-energy flavor observables ($q^2$-binned decay rate and $A_{FB}$ in $D\to K\mu\nu$) and high-energy collider constraints (LHC bounds on high-$p_T$ Drell-Yan tail), including consistency checks for complex NP Wilson coefficients in semileptonic $c\to s\ell\nu$ transitions.
