title: Probing Unruh Effect from Enhanced Decoherence
summary: We investigate the decoherence of an Unruh-DeWitt detector coupled to scalar, electromagnetic, and spinor fields in four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime. By employing the Schwinger-Keldysh influence functional formalism, we derive a universal scaling law relating the decoherence rate to the proper acceleration $a$ and the scaling dimension $Δ$ of the environmental field operator. By analyzing both sharp (top-hat) and smooth Gaussian switching functions, it is shown that the decoherence rate in the asymptotic long-time limit scales as $a^{2Δ-1}$. This scaling indicates that increasing scaling dimension of the coupling field operators can significantly enhance the decoherence, thereby providing a more sensitive probe of the Unruh effect.

AI.tldr: This paper derives a universal scaling law for the decoherence rate of an Unruh-DeWitt detector coupled to quantum fields in Minkowski spacetime, showing it scales as $a^{2\Delta-1}$ with proper acceleration $a$ and field operator scaling dimension $\Delta$, enhancing sensitivity to the Unruh effect.
AI.motivation: To quantify and understand how field operator scaling dimension affects decoherence of accelerated detectors, thereby improving detection sensitivity to the Unruh effect.
AI.method: Schwinger-Keldysh influence functional formalism applied to Unruh-DeWitt detectors coupled to scalar, electromagnetic, and spinor fields; analysis with sharp (top-hat) and smooth Gaussian switching functions.
AI.result: Decoherence rate in the asymptotic long-time limit universally scales as $a^{2\Delta-1}$, independent of field spin or specific switching profile in the long-time limit.
AI.conclusion: Higher scaling dimension $\Delta$ of the coupled field operator strongly enhances decoherence, making such detectors more effective probes of the Unruh effect.

title: Efficient computation of the N-th rank QED polarization tensor: Universal worldline structure of form factors
comment: 70 pages, 2 figures. The ancillary file headgen.py contains the computer script accompanying this manuscript
summary: We derived in arXiv:2206.04188 arXiv:2211.15712 a compact expression for the $N$-th rank QED polarization tensor $Π_{μ_1\cdots μ_N}(k_1,\cdots,k_N)$ in a $(0+1)$-dimensional worldline framework. This fully off-shell object, a function of $N$ external photon four-momenta, is a key ingredient in high-order computations of cusp anomalous dimensions and lepton anomalous magnetic moments. We demonstrate here that $Π_{μ_1\cdots μ_N}$ can further be expressed simply in terms of a small number of independent ``head" form factors (each representing $(N-1)!/2$ Feynman diagrams) which have a universal structure in terms of sums over fermion Green functions and (propertime derivative of) their boson worldline superpartners. This worldline representation bypasses explicit Wick contractions and avoids tensor reductions to scalar loop integrals à la Passarino and Veltman, order by order in perturbation theory. We give explicit expressions for the $4$-th and $6$-th rank head form factors and provide a computer script generalizing these results to arbitrary $N$ external photons. The multiplicity of heads, and their growth with $N$, can be understood in terms of orbits of the permutation group. We employ the Burnside-Cauchy-Frobenius lemma to show that it scales as $e^{N-1}/\sqrt{N}$ terms as opposed to the $e^{N-1} N!/\sqrt{N}$ terms in conventional perturbation theory. We reexpress worldline parameter integrals that define the $4$-th rank heads as Feynman parameter integrals to reproduce the seminal results by Karplus and Neuman for the on-shell light-by-light amplitude and extend these to the fully off-shell case in massless QED employing a tailored integration-by-parts procedure. In a follow-up paper, we will discuss the direct computation of worldline integrals, potentially providing a further $N!$ advantage relative to Feynman diagram computations at high orders in perturbation theory.

AI.tldr: This paper reformulates the N-th rank QED polarization tensor using a (0+1)-dimensional worldline framework, introducing compact 'head' form factors that encode symmetry-reduced contributions—reducing computational complexity from ~N! to ~e^{N−1}/√N via group-theoretic orbit counting—and provides explicit 4th/6th-rank results plus automated code.
AI.motivation: To overcome combinatorial explosion and tensor reduction bottlenecks in high-order QED calculations (e.g., cusp anomalous dimensions, lepton g−2), especially for fully off-shell N-photon amplitudes.
AI.method: Uses a (0+1)D worldline formalism to represent the N-point polarization tensor Π_{μ₁⋯μ_N} via symmetry-organized 'head' form factors; applies Burnside-Cauchy-Frobenius lemma to count independent heads; rewrites worldline integrals as Feynman-parameter forms to recover and extend Karplus–Neuman results; includes automated symbolic computation.
AI.result: Derives compact universal expressions for 4th- and 6th-rank head form factors; proves asymptotic head count scales as e^{N−1}/√N (vs. e^{N−1}N!/√N in standard perturbation theory); reproduces on-shell light-by-light scattering and extends it fully off-shell in massless QED; provides publicly usable code for arbitrary N.
AI.conclusion: The worldline 'head' decomposition offers exponential (N!) computational advantage over conventional Feynman diagrammatics for high-N QED amplitudes, enabling feasible all-order studies of off-shell multi-photon processes and precision observables.

title: Orthogonal pairs of Euler elements II: Geometric Bisognano--Wichmann and Spin--Statistics Theorems
summary:
Models in Algebraic Quantum Field Theory (AQFT) may be generalized including Lie groups of symmetries whose Lie algebras admit an Euler element $h$, characterized by the property that $ad h$ is diagonalizable with eigenvalues in $\{-1, 0, 1\}$. These elements becomes fundamental to the formal description of wedge localization. In this paper, we extend the geometric analysis of Euler wedges and investigate their applications within the AQFT framework.
  We call a pair of Euler elements $(h, k)$ orthogonal if
  $e^{i π\operatorname{ad} h}(k) = -k.$ Using the geometric framework established in our previous work, we derive both a Bisognano--Wichmann Theorem and a Spin--Statistics Theorem for nets of standard subspaces and von Neumann algebras. Our results {show} how this generalized approach recovers classical results in the AQFT literature while providing a deeper structural understanding of the underlying geometry in established models.

AI.tldr: This paper generalizes AQFT models using Euler elements in Lie algebras to describe wedge localization; it introduces orthogonal Euler elements, proves generalized Bisognano–Wichmann and Spin–Statistics theorems for standard subspaces and von Neumann algebras, and unifies classical results with deeper geometric insight.
AI.motivation: To extend AQFT's geometric foundation by incorporating Lie algebras with Euler elements—enabling a more structural and unified description of wedge localization and symmetry properties beyond standard Minkowski spacetime settings.
AI.method: Geometric analysis of Euler wedges using Lie-theoretic tools; definition and exploitation of orthogonality between Euler elements via adjoint action; derivation of modular covariance (Bisognano–Wichmann) and spin-statistics correspondence for nets of standard subspaces and associated von Neumann algebras.
AI.result: Proof of a generalized Bisognano–Wichmann Theorem and a generalized Spin–Statistics Theorem within the Euler-element framework; demonstration that classical AQFT results emerge as special cases; establishment of a geometric characterization of wedge duality and modular flow in terms of Euler elements.
AI.conclusion: Euler elements provide a natural and powerful algebraic–geometric framework for wedge localization in AQFT; orthogonality of Euler elements encodes key physical structures (e.g., causality, duality, statistics), yielding both conceptual unification and technical generalization of foundational theorems.

title: Magnetic Weyl Super Calculus: Schatten-class properties, commutator criterion, and complete positivity
summary:
We combine our previous results on magnetic pseudo-differential operators for Hörmander symbols dominated by tempered weights [arXiv:2511.07184] with the magnetic Weyl super calculus of Lee and Lein [arXiv:2201.11487, arXiv:2405.19964]. This allows us to extend some previous results on the semi-super and super Moyal algebra, as well as to prove boundedness, compactness, and Schatten-class properties of super operators.
  Moreover, we prove a Beals-type commutator criterion for super operators and we also formulate sufficient conditions on super symbols in order to give rise to completely positive and trace preserving maps.
  For most of the proofs we use decompositions of operators and super operators based on Parseval frames of smoothing operators.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the theory of magnetic pseudo-differential operators and magnetic Weyl super calculus to establish boundedness, compactness, Schatten-class membership, a Beals-type commutator criterion, and sufficient conditions for complete positivity and trace preservation of super operators—using Parseval frame decompositions of smoothing operators.
AI.motivation: To unify and extend existing frameworks—namely magnetic pseudo-differential calculus for tempered-weight Hörmander symbols and magnetic Weyl super calculus—to rigorously analyze functional-analytic and quantum-dynamical properties of super operators.
AI.method: Combines magnetic pseudo-differential operator theory with magnetic Weyl super calculus; employs Parseval frame decompositions of smoothing operators as the primary technical tool for proofs.
AI.result: Extended semi-super and super Moyal algebras; proved boundedness, compactness, and Schatten-class properties of super operators; established a Beals-type commutator criterion for super operators; derived sufficient symbol conditions for completely positive and trace-preserving (CPTP) maps.
AI.conclusion: The unified framework enables rigorous analysis of quantum dynamical maps and operator-theoretic properties in magnetic and supersymmetric settings, with implications for open quantum systems and noncommutative harmonic analysis.

title: Circular orbits in spherically symmetric spacetimes and BSW effect with nonzero force
summary: We consider circular particle motion under the action of an unspecified force in a static spherically symmetric spacetime. We derive the machinery that allows one to find the force acting on a circular particle and deduce whether its position is stable or not. This also allows one to extend the definition of ISCO to the case of a non-zero external force. By conducting the near-horizon expansion, we obtain that for any non-extremal black holes, the acceleration for extremal ones is finite, and for ultraextremal (multiple) horizons it tends to zero. Applying the derived machinery to the case of the Schwarzschild metric assuming that a force is constant, we scrutiny how the number of orbits for a given force depends on its value. In particular, if a force is big enough, an additional branch of solutions appears that was absent in the case of geodesic motion. Then, for various circular orbits, we numerically investigate their stability. A similar problem is solved for the Reissner-Nordstrom (RN) metric and uncharged particles. It appears that for the near-extremal and extremal RN black holes, there exist near-horizon circle trajectories (in contrast to the nonextremal case). For the ISCO, the dependence of the orbit radius on $κ$ (the surface gravity) is similar to that in the case of neutral particles moving in the background of rotating black holes. In addition, two scenarios of high-energy particle collisions near such orbits are considered, and it is found that dependence on $κ$ is also similar to that for rotating black holes.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a general framework for analyzing circular particle motion under arbitrary external forces in static, spherically symmetric spacetimes, extends the ISCO concept to forced motion, and applies it to Schwarzschild and Reissner–Nordström black holes—revealing new orbit branches, near-horizon trajectories for extremal RN black holes, and universal κ-dependence of ISCO radius and high-energy collision energy resembling that of rotating black holes.
AI.motivation: To generalize orbital mechanics beyond geodesic motion by incorporating unspecified external forces, extend the ISCO concept to forced circular orbits, and explore how force alters stability, orbit multiplicity, and near-horizon dynamics—especially in extremal and ultraextremal black hole spacetimes.
AI.method: Derives general conditions for circular orbits under arbitrary radial forces in static spherically symmetric spacetimes; performs near-horizon asymptotic expansions of acceleration; analytically and numerically solves for circular orbits and their stability (via effective potential second-derivative analysis) in Schwarzschild (constant-force case) and Reissner–Nordström (uncharged particles) metrics; examines high-energy particle collisions near forced ISCOs.
AI.result: 1) A general formalism for forced circular orbits and stability criterion is established; 2) For Schwarzschild with constant force, a new branch of stable orbits emerges above a critical force threshold; 3) Near-horizon circular orbits exist for extremal and near-extremal RN black holes, absent in nonextremal cases; 4) ISCO radius and center-of-mass energy of colliding particles scale similarly with surface gravity κ as in Kerr black holes.
AI.conclusion: External forces qualitatively enrich orbital structure—inducing new stable orbits, enabling near-horizon circular motion in extremal electrovacuum black holes, and yielding universal κ-scaling laws for ISCO and collision energy that bridge nonrotating and rotating black hole physics.

title: Same-sign dimuon probe of charged lepton flavor violation at electron-photon colliders
summary: Observation of charged lepton flavor violation would constitute unambiguous evidence for physics beyond the Standard Model (SM). We identify a previously unexplored same-sign dimuon signature in electron-photon collisions, $γe^- \to e^+μ^-μ^-$, mediated by an axionlike particle (ALP) with flavor-violating $e$-$μ$ couplings. The absence of irreducible SM backgrounds and the on-shell production of the ALP render this channel intrinsically clean and highly sensitive, with only small residual backgrounds arising from detector effects. Such collisions can be realized via laser Compton backscattering at $e^+e^-$ colliders including BEPC-II with the BESIII detector, STCF, and ILC. We find that STCF and ILC can probe couplings one to two orders of magnitude below existing bounds. This combination of resonant production, vanishing irreducible background, and same-sign topology would be difficult to achieve in conventional $e^+e^-$ or hadron-collider environments, establishing electron-photon collisions as a uniquely powerful probe of charged lepton flavor violation.

AI.tldr: Proposes a novel same-sign dimuon signature (γe⁻ → e⁺μ⁻μ⁻) in electron-photon collisions to probe charged lepton flavor violation via on-shell axionlike particles (ALPs) with e–μ couplings; offers negligible SM background, resonant sensitivity, and improved reach at STCF/ILC over current limits.
AI.motivation: Charged lepton flavor violation (cLFV) is a smoking-gun signal of physics beyond the Standard Model; existing searches lack clean channels with resonant production and no irreducible SM background.
AI.method: Theoretical analysis of γe⁻ → e⁺μ⁻μ⁻ process mediated by an on-shell axionlike particle (ALP) with flavor-violating e–μ couplings; background estimation including detector effects; collider feasibility assessment using laser Compton backscattering at BEPC-II/BESIII, STCF, and ILC.
AI.result: STCF and ILC can probe ALP e–μ couplings one to two orders of magnitude below current experimental bounds; the channel has vanishing irreducible SM background and high sensitivity due to resonant ALP production and same-sign dimuon topology.
AI.conclusion: Electron-photon collisions provide a uniquely clean and sensitive probe of cLFV—superior to conventional e⁺e⁻ or hadron colliders—due to resonant ALP production, absence of irreducible backgrounds, and distinctive same-sign dimuon signature.

title: Simulation-based Inference towards Gravitational-wave waveform systematics in Intermediate-Mass Binary Black Holes
summary:
Parameter estimation for gravitational-wave signals is computationally demanding due to the high dimensionality of the parameter space and the cost of repeated waveform generation in traditional Bayesian inference. These analyses require on the order of 10^8 likelihood evaluations and waveform generations, resulting in inference times of hours to days per event. Furthermore, discrepancies between waveform models introduce systematic uncertainties that can bias inferred source properties. To address these challenges, we propose a novel framework based on Simulation-based Inference (SBI) and Neural Posterior Estimation (NPE) and apply it to signals from Intermediate-Mass Black Holes (IMBH). In this framework, we train a single amortised neural posterior estimator on a large simulated dataset generated using two state-of-the-art waveform approximants, IMRPhenomXPHM and SEOBNRv5PHM. By treating the waveform model index as a latent variable, the network learns to produce posterior distributions that are naturally marginalized over the discrepancies of the two waveform models. Once trained, the model enables direct posterior sampling in milliseconds per event, eliminating the need for likelihood evaluations while simultaneously accounting for model systematics.
  We demonstrate that this approach recovers accurate posterior distributions for IMBH signals injected into Gaussian noise, achieving close agreement with traditional nested-sampling results while reducing inference time by several orders of magnitude. Our results show that NPE can robustly incorporate waveform-model systematics within a unified framework, offering a scalable path toward rapid, systematics-aware gravitational-wave inference. Establishing these methods as promising alternatives to classical likelihood-based pipelines for current and future high-mass gravitational-wave observations.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a Simulation-based Inference (SBI) framework using Neural Posterior Estimation (NPE) to accelerate gravitational-wave parameter estimation for Intermediate-Mass Black Hole (IMBH) signals, while marginalizing over waveform model uncertainty—achieving millisecond inference per event with accuracy matching traditional nested sampling.
AI.motivation: High computational cost of Bayesian inference (10^8 likelihood evaluations, hours–days per event) and systematic biases from waveform model discrepancies in gravitational-wave parameter estimation.
AI.method: Amortized neural posterior estimator trained on simulated IMBH signals generated with two state-of-the-art waveform models (IMRPhenomXPHM and SEOBNRv5PHM); waveform model index treated as latent variable to enable automatic marginalization over model uncertainty.
AI.result: Accurate posterior recovery on IMBH injections in Gaussian noise, matching nested-sampling results; inference time reduced to milliseconds per event; robust handling of waveform-model systematics.
AI.conclusion: NPE-based SBI provides a scalable, rapid, and systematics-aware alternative to classical likelihood-based pipelines for high-mass gravitational-wave inference.

title: A Resonance in Elastic Kink-Meson Scattering
summary: We analytically sum the leading bubble diagrams that contribute to the elastic scattering amplitude of a kink and a meson in the $φ^4$ double-well model. We find a single peak, corresponding to the unstable kink state in which the shape mode is excited twice. The peak has the usual Breit-Wigner form, and its imaginary part agrees with the shape mode decay rate found by Manton and Merabet.

AI.tldr: Analytically sums leading bubble diagrams for kink-meson elastic scattering in the φ⁴ double-well model, revealing a Breit-Wigner resonance corresponding to double excitation of the shape mode; its width matches the known decay rate by Manton and Merabet.
AI.motivation: To understand the resonance structure and decay dynamics of unstable kink states in the φ⁴ model, particularly how shape-mode excitations manifest in scattering amplitudes.
AI.method: Analytic summation of leading bubble diagram contributions to the kink–meson elastic scattering amplitude within the φ⁴ double-well quantum field theory.
AI.result: A single Breit-Wigner resonance peak is found, associated with double excitation of the kink's shape mode; its imaginary part (width) quantitatively agrees with the shape mode decay rate computed earlier by Manton and Merabet.
AI.conclusion: The unstable kink state with two quanta of shape-mode excitation forms a well-defined resonance in kink–meson scattering, and its lifetime is fully captured by the established shape-mode decay rate.

title: Cosmological Correlators Using Tensor Networks
summary: We develop a nonperturbative tensor-network framework for computing cosmological correlators in de Sitter space and use it to test the proposal that suitably defined in-in correlators can be obtained from an in-out formalism by gluing the expanding and contracting Poincaré patches. Focusing on interacting $1+1$-dimensional $φ^4$ theory, we formulate finite-time lattice observables using Matrix Product State (MPS) techniques and analyze the regulator subtleties associated with the singular behavior near the patching surface. Within this regulated framework, we find controlled nonperturbative evidence for the proposed relation between in-in and in-out correlators in several examples. We also find suggestive evidence that the perturbative obstructions present for sufficiently light fields can be softened nonperturbatively, albeit in a regime of substantially larger entanglement. A central outcome of our analysis is an entanglement-based picture of the computation: for in-in evolution the entanglement remains modest and can decrease toward late times, whereas in the patched in-out set-up it grows significantly after the gluing slice. Thus, although the in-out formalism is perturbatively economical, the in-in formulation is numerically more favorable. We briefly discuss how the same strategy extends to low-angular-momentum sectors in $3+1$ dimensions, and why regimes of rapid entanglement growth may eventually motivate quantum-computing implementations.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a nonperturbative tensor-network (MPS) framework to compute cosmological correlators in de Sitter space, testing the conjecture that in-in correlators can be derived from an in-out formalism via gluing expanding/contracting Poincaré patches; it finds controlled nonperturbative support for this relation in 1+1D φ⁴ theory, reveals an entanglement-based trade-off (in-in has modest/decreasing entanglement, patched in-out exhibits large growth post-gluing), and suggests quantum computing may be needed where entanglement grows rapidly.
AI.motivation: To nonperturbatively test the conjectured equivalence between in-in correlators (standard for cosmology) and a glued in-out formalism in de Sitter space—motivated by potential computational simplifications but challenged by regulator subtleties and perturbative obstructions for light fields.
AI.method: Develops a finite-time lattice formulation using Matrix Product States (MPS) for interacting 1+1D φ⁴ theory in de Sitter; carefully regulates singularities near the patching surface; computes and compares in-in and patched in-out correlators; analyzes entanglement dynamics across time evolution and gluing.
AI.result: Finds controlled nonperturbative evidence supporting the in-in / glued in-out correlator relation; observes that perturbative obstructions for light fields are softened nonperturbatively (though at cost of higher entanglement); identifies stark entanglement contrast: in-in evolution maintains modest or decreasing entanglement, while patched in-out shows sharp entanglement growth after gluing.
AI.conclusion: The in-in formalism is numerically more favorable despite perturbative inefficiency, due to its benign entanglement scaling; the patched in-out approach, while perturbatively economical, incurs high entanglement costs; this entanglement-based insight motivates future quantum simulation for high-entanglement regimes, and the framework extends to low-ℓ sectors in 3+1D.

title: Complete Next-to-Next-to-Leading-Order QCD Correction to $J/ψ\to 3γ$ Decay
summary: We address the long-standing problem of negative decay and production rates in perturbative QCD for exclusive processes by proposing amplitude-level NRQCD factorization as a systematic prescription. Building on this, we present the first complete next-to-next-to-leading-order (NNLO) QCD correction to the decay $J/ψ\to 3γ$. The resulting partial width, $Γ(J/ψ\to 3γ) = 0.96^{+4.32}_{-0.13}$ eV, combines this NNLO contribution with the known up to $\mathcal{O}(α_s v^2)$ relativistic correction and shows markedly improved agreement with the high-precision BESIII measurement. In the same way, $Γ(Υ\to 3γ) = 0.0086^{+0.0028}_{-0.0006}$ eV is obtained. The dominant theoretical uncertainty originates from the renormalization scale variation, underscoring the challenge of perturbative convergence at this order and the necessity for future higher-order calculations.

AI.tldr: This paper resolves negative decay/production rates in perturbative QCD for exclusive processes via amplitude-level NRQCD factorization, and reports the first complete NNLO QCD calculation for J/ψ → 3γ decay, yielding Γ = 0.96^{+4.32}_{−0.13} eV — significantly improving agreement with BESIII data; analogous result for Υ → 3γ is also given.
AI.motivation: To resolve the long-standing issue of unphysical (negative) decay and production rates in perturbative QCD predictions for exclusive heavy quarkonium processes, arising from poor convergence and inconsistent treatment of relativistic and QCD corrections.
AI.method: Introduces amplitude-level NRQCD factorization as a systematic framework; computes the full NNLO QCD correction to J/ψ → 3γ decay amplitude, consistently combining it with known O(α_s v^2) relativistic corrections; applies same method to Υ → 3γ.
AI.result: Γ(J/ψ → 3γ) = 0.96^{+4.32}_{−0.13} eV; Γ(Υ → 3γ) = 0.0086^{+0.0028}_{−0.0006} eV; both show improved agreement with experiment (especially BESIII), though scale uncertainty dominates theoretical error, indicating limited perturbative convergence at NNLO.
AI.conclusion: Amplitude-level NRQCD factorization eliminates unphysical predictions and enables robust higher-order calculations; the NNLO result for J/ψ → 3γ marks a milestone in precision quarkonium physics, but further higher-order (e.g., N3LO) or resummation efforts are needed to control scale dependence and improve reliability.

title: EVERY CFT$_3$ HAS AN $ \mathcal{L}_Λw_{1+\infty}$ SYMMETRY
summary: Recently a one-parameter family of deformed $ \mathcal{L} w_{1+\infty}$ soft symmetry algebras, denoted $ \mathcal{L}_Λw_{1+\infty}$, acting on tree-level gravitational theories in AdS$_4$ has been discovered. Here we show that all CFT$_3$s, including those dual to quantum gravity on AdS$_4$, admit an $\mathcal{L}_Λw_{1+\infty}$ action generated by the ANEC operator, its conformal descendants and their commutators. This extends the previous tree-level results on these soft symmetries to the strongly-coupled quantum regime.

AI.tldr: Extends the deformed soft symmetry algebra $\mathcal{L}_\Lambda w_{1+\infty}$ from tree-level AdS$_4$ gravity to all 3D CFTs—including strongly-coupled ones—via ANEC and its descendants.
AI.motivation: To generalize previously established tree-level soft symmetries in AdS$_4$/CFT$_3$ to the full quantum regime, including strongly-coupled CFTs dual to quantum gravity.
AI.method: Constructs the $\mathcal{L}_\Lambda w_{1+\infty}$ algebra on arbitrary 3D CFTs using the ANEC operator, its conformal descendants, and nested commutators—without relying on weak-coupling or semiclassical gravity assumptions.
AI.result: Proves that every 3D CFT admits an $\mathcal{L}_\Lambda w_{1+\infty}$ symmetry action, thereby lifting the earlier AdS$_4$ tree-level result to the fully quantum, non-perturbative level.
AI.conclusion: The $\mathcal{L}_\Lambda w_{1+\infty}$ soft symmetry is universal across all 3D CFTs, not merely a feature of perturbative gravity; it is intrinsically encoded in the ANEC and conformal structure.

title: Electromagnetic radiation mediated by topological surface states
comment: Accepted for publication in the Physical Review D
summary: We study electromagnetic radiation from classical sources near a planar interface separating a topological and a trivial insulator, modeled within axion electrodynamics. The system features a piecewise constant $θ$-term that encodes the magnetoelectric response of topological surface states. Treating this coupling perturbatively, we derive analytical corrections to the standard Liénard-Wiechert potentials and obtain modified radiation fields in the far zone. As applications, we analyze the emission from linear antennas and the bremsstrahlung radiation of accelerated charges near the interface. For antennas, the surface Hall response breaks axial symmetry and produces azimuthal modulations that grow with the electrical length, leading to distinct scaling behaviors in the total and angular radiated power. {For accelerated charges, the emitted intensity is uniformly reduced by a factor $1 - (σ_{\mathrm{Hall}} / 2εv)^2$, which we interpret as a process-specific attenuation of the radiative strength due to interference with its image magnetic monopole inside the topological medium.} These results reveal how topological surface states mediate measurable modifications to classical radiation, establishing a link between axion electrodynamics, topological phases, and field theories with spatially varying couplings.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates electromagnetic radiation from classical sources near an interface between a topological and a trivial insulator using axion electrodynamics, deriving analytical corrections to Liénard–Wiechert potentials and predicting measurable modifications—such as azimuthal power modulation for antennas and Hall-induced attenuation of bremsstrahlung—due to the surface Hall response.
AI.motivation: To understand how topological surface states, encoded via a piecewise-constant axion angle θ in axion electrodynamics, modify classical electromagnetic radiation from sources near a topological–trivial insulator interface.
AI.method: Perturbative treatment of the θ-term coupling; derivation of corrected Liénard–Wiechert potentials and far-zone radiation fields; analytical analysis of antenna radiation and bremsstrahlung near the interface.
AI.result: 1) Antennas exhibit azimuthally modulated radiation patterns with scaling distinct from conventional cases due to broken axial symmetry from surface Hall conductivity; 2) Bremsstrahlung intensity is uniformly reduced by factor 1 − (σ_Hall / 2εv)², interpreted as interference with an image magnetic monopole induced in the topological medium.
AI.conclusion: Topological surface states induce quantifiable, process-dependent modifications to classical radiation, bridging axion electrodynamics, topological phases, and spatially inhomogeneous field theories.

title: (3+1)D dilute Glasma initial conditions in simulations of heavy-ion collisions
comment: PhD Thesis, 217 pages, 43 figures, 4 tables. Abstract shortened to comply with arXiv guidelines. Supplemental material, raw data, raw plots, and plot scripts available from https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18242275
summary: In this thesis, an approximation for the full (3+1)D dynamics of the Glasma is presented, which breaks boost-invariance on the level of the nuclear fields and leads to rapidity dependence in the final results. For this treatment, the Yang-Mills equations are linearized in covariant gauge, where lower-order, nonlinear contributions are neglected and the dynamics are captured by the (3+1)D dilute Glasma. The analytic solutions of the (3+1)D dilute Glasma are derived in both position and momentum space formulations, providing a comprehensive understanding of the involved (3+1)D dynamics. In position space, the field strength tensor results from the integration of free-streaming gluons that are produced in $2\rightarrow1$ scattering processes where the initial nuclear fields overlap. In momentum space, the event-averaged gluon number distribution for the (3+1)D dilute Glasma is derived in Coulomb gauge. A generalized, three-dimensional McLerran-Venugopalan nuclear model is developed for nuclei with realistic envelopes and intrinsic longitudinal correlations. Numerical results are presented for the rapidity structure of the energy-momentum tensor, the gluon number distribution, and the transverse energy of the (3+1)D dilute Glasma. In position space, the extended longitudinal collision geometry and finite longitudinal correlation length break boost-invariance. In momentum space, the results each follow universal parametrizations and are fixed by the values of two scaling parameters. Furthermore, the numerical results exhibit limiting fragmentation where the rapidity profiles approach a limiting distribution at large rapidities. This feature is also derived locally in position space for the analytic expressions of the field strength tensor and, in momentum space, for the transverse energy of the (3+1)D dilute Glasma.

AI.tldr: This thesis develops a (3+1)D dilute Glasma framework that breaks boost-invariance by incorporating realistic nuclear structure—finite longitudinal correlation length and extended collision geometry—yielding rapidity-dependent analytic solutions for field strength (position space) and gluon distribution (momentum space), with numerical results showing limiting fragmentation.
AI.motivation: To go beyond boost-invariant approximations in Glasma dynamics by incorporating realistic nuclear geometry and longitudinal correlations, enabling description of rapidity-dependent observables in high-energy heavy-ion collisions.
AI.method: Linearization of Yang-Mills equations in covariant gauge (dilute limit); analytic solution of (3+1)D Glasma in position space (free-streaming gluons from 2→1 scattering) and momentum space (Coulomb-gauge event-averaged gluon spectrum); development of a generalized 3D McLerran-Venugopalan model with realistic nuclear envelopes and intrinsic longitudinal correlations.
AI.result: Analytic expressions for field strength tensor (position space) and event-averaged gluon number distribution (momentum space); numerical rapidity profiles of energy-momentum tensor, gluon density, and transverse energy; demonstration of limiting fragmentation both numerically and analytically (locally in position space for field strength, and in momentum space for transverse energy); universal scaling governed by two parameters.
AI.conclusion: The (3+1)D dilute Glasma framework successfully captures rapidity dependence and limiting fragmentation without boost-invariance, providing a more realistic foundation for early-time dynamics in heavy-ion collisions, with predictions constrained by two universal scaling parameters.

title: Complex bumblebee model
summary: We formulate a renormalizable complex extension of the bumblebee theory in which the bumblebee field is promoted to a complex one and coupled to an Abelian gauge sector. Besides the minimal gauge covariant interaction, the model includes a longitudinal kinetic term controlled by a dimensionless parameter $g_l$ and a non-minimal magnetic-type coupling $g_m$ between the complex bumblebee and the photon. Using dimensional regularization and minimal subtraction, we determine the one-loop UV divergences of the two-, three-, and four-point functions relevant to the renormalization of the gauge, longitudinal, and quartic sectors. We obtain the corresponding counterterms and derive the one-loop renormalization-group functions for $e$, $g_l$, $g_m$, and the bumblebee self-couplings $λ$ and $\tildeλ$. Motivated by the known gauge- and field-reparametrization subtleties of the conventional Coleman--Weinberg analysis, we formulate an RG-covariant leading-logarithmic improvement scheme for the Vilkovisky--DeWitt effective potential in normal field coordinates, in which the RG operator is governed solely by the beta functions. We apply this framework to a real constant bumblebee background and obtain the leading-logarithmic one-loop effective potential, discussing the conditions under which a nontrivial vacuum is generated by dimensional transmutation and thereby provides a dynamical realization of Lorentz symmetry breaking in this class of models.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a renormalizable complex extension of the bumblebee model coupled to an Abelian gauge field, computes its one-loop UV divergences and RG functions, and develops an RG-covariant effective potential formalism to study dynamical Lorentz violation via dimensional transmutation.
AI.motivation: To construct a consistent, renormalizable quantum field theory incorporating spontaneous Lorentz symmetry breaking (via a complex bumblebee field), while addressing technical challenges in effective potential calculations—particularly gauge and field-reparametrization dependence in conventional Coleman–Weinberg approaches.
AI.method: Dimensional regularization with minimal subtraction; computation of one-loop UV divergences for two-, three-, and four-point functions; derivation of beta functions for couplings (e, g_l, g_m, λ, λ̃); formulation of an RG-covariant leading-logarithmic improvement scheme for the Vilkovisky–DeWitt effective potential in normal field coordinates.
AI.result: Complete set of one-loop counterterms and beta functions for all couplings; RG-covariant leading-logarithmic effective potential for a real constant bumblebee background; identification of parameter regimes where dimensional transmutation generates a nontrivial vacuum and thus dynamical Lorentz violation.
AI.conclusion: The complex bumblebee–QED extension is perturbatively renormalizable at one loop; its RG-improved effective potential supports spontaneous Lorentz breaking through dimensional transmutation, offering a consistent quantum framework for dynamical symmetry breaking beyond standard Higgs mechanisms.

title: Constraints on axion-like particles via associated diboson production in hadronic collisions
summary: We investigate the sensitivity of current and future hadron-collider experiments to axion-like particles (ALPs) through associated diboson production, focusing on a linear effective field theory framework with bosonic ALP couplings. We analyze the dominant production mechanisms and relevant backgrounds, considering the impact of jet misidentification rates on the diboson background. We present our results using conservative jet-misidentification rates, and derive four dimensional constraints on the ALP couplings to gluons, weak bosons, and photons. Our findings highlight the potential of the high-luminosity phase of the CERN Large Hadron Collider to probe the ALP parameter space in the sub-GeV mass range, as well as the codependencies of the various ALP couplings.

AI.tldr: This paper studies ALP sensitivity at hadron colliders via diboson production in a linear EFT framework, deriving 4D coupling constraints using conservative jet-misidentification rates; it emphasizes HL-LHC’s capability to probe sub-GeV ALPs and coupling degeneracies.
AI.motivation: To assess current and future hadron-collider sensitivity to axion-like particles (ALPs) — particularly in the sub-GeV mass range — via associated diboson production, leveraging an effective field theory approach with bosonic ALP couplings.
AI.method: Analyzes dominant ALP-associated diboson production mechanisms and backgrounds within a linear bosonic EFT; incorporates realistic jet misidentification rates to model diboson background; derives four-dimensional constraints on ALP couplings to gluons, weak bosons, and photons.
AI.result: Derives quantitative 4D exclusion limits on ALP couplings; demonstrates that HL-LHC can significantly probe sub-GeV ALPs; reveals strong codependencies among gluonic, electroweak, and photonic ALP couplings.
AI.conclusion: HL-LHC offers compelling discovery potential for light ALPs through diboson channels; full interpretation requires joint treatment of multiple ALP couplings due to parameter degeneracies; jet-misidentification modeling is critical for robust background estimation.

title: Implication of dressed form of relational observable on von Neumann algebra
summary: In quantum gravity, physically meaningful operator is required to be invariant under the diffeomorphisms. Such gauge invariant operator is typically given by the relational observable, the operator localized in relation to some background states. We point out that the relational observable can be comprehensively written in the form of the dressed operator. For the background having boundary where the diffeomorphisms are not gauged, we can use the gravitational Wilson line for dressing, then the relational observable is nonlocal. In contrast, when the background breaks some isometries, as can be found in quasi-de Sitter space, dressing can be local, which is a kind of Stückelberg mechanism. Since dressing resembles the outer automorphism in the von Neumann algebra, we may investigate the algebraic structure of the background by considering the dressed form of the relational observable. From this, we can understand that quasi-de Sitter space is described by the Type II$_\infty$ algebra where the trace diverges in the decoupling limit of gravity. It is different from the Type II$_1$ algebra of de Sitter space where the finite size of trace can be defined in the same limit. This shows that the isometry preserving and breaking backgrounds are quite different in the algebraic structure no matter how small the breaking effect is.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a unified framework for relational observables in quantum gravity using 'dressed operators', distinguishing between nonlocal (e.g., boundary-based) and local (e.g., Stückelberg-type) dressing; it further classifies quasi-de Sitter and de Sitter backgrounds via von Neumann algebra types (II∞ vs. II₁), revealing a qualitative algebraic distinction tied to isometry breaking—even infinitesimally.
AI.motivation: To construct physically meaningful, diffeomorphism-invariant observables in quantum gravity—specifically relational observables—and to understand how their mathematical structure (especially dressing and algebraic type) depends on background geometry and symmetry properties.
AI.method: Formulates relational observables as dressed operators; employs gravitational Wilson lines for dressing in boundary-anchored backgrounds and local Stückelberg-like dressing in isometry-breaking backgrounds (e.g., quasi-de Sitter); analyzes the resulting operator algebras using von Neumann algebra theory, particularly trace classification in the gravity decoupling limit.
AI.result: Relational observables admit a universal dressed-operator representation; dressing locality depends critically on background isometries; quasi-de Sitter space corresponds to a Type II∞ von Neumann algebra (divergent trace), whereas exact de Sitter yields Type II₁ (finite trace)—a sharp algebraic distinction persisting even under arbitrarily small isometry breaking.
AI.conclusion: The algebraic structure of quantum gravitational observables—encoded in the von Neumann type—is topologically sensitive to background isometries: isometry breaking induces a phase transition from Type II₁ to Type II∞, implying that quasi-de Sitter and de Sitter are fundamentally distinct quantum gravitational backgrounds, not mere perturbations.

title: Non-eikonal corrections to dijet production in DIS
summary: We compute non-eikonal corrections to dijet production in deep inelastic scattering off a nucleus. Such corrections are expected to be quantitatively important at the energies of the future Electron Ion Collider. We focus on those corrections stemming solely from the finite longitudinal size of the nucleus. For both longitudinally and transversely polarized photons, we provide general, all-order expressions in terms of two-dimensional path integrals. To proceed further, we use the harmonic oscillator approximation for the target averages of Wilson lines. We then expand the general expressions order by order beyond the shockwave limit which provides the eikonal results, up to next-to-next-to-eikonal accuracy. We observe that next-to-eikonal corrections to this observable vanish for the mentioned approximation for target averages, as previously found for single gluon production in proton-nucleus collisions. Finally, we calculate the back-to-back of correlation limit of our expressions.

AI.tldr: This paper computes non-eikonal corrections to dijet production in deep inelastic scattering off a nucleus, focusing on finite longitudinal nuclear size effects; it derives all-order 2D path-integral expressions for both photon polarizations, applies the harmonic oscillator model for Wilson line averages, expands beyond the shockwave (eikonal) limit up to NNLO in the eikonal expansion, finds NLO corrections vanish under this approximation (as in prior p+A gluon production), and evaluates the back-to-back correlation limit.
AI.motivation: Non-eikonal corrections are expected to be quantitatively important at Electron Ion Collider energies, especially those arising from the finite longitudinal size of the nucleus, which are neglected in the standard eikonal (shockwave) approximation.
AI.method: Derives general all-order expressions for dijet production using two-dimensional path integrals over Wilson lines; employs the harmonic oscillator approximation for target-averaged Wilson line correlators; performs systematic expansion beyond the shockwave limit up to next-to-next-to-eikonal (NNN? — clarified as NN-eikonal) order; analyzes the back-to-back correlation limit.
AI.result: Next-to-eikonal (NE) corrections vanish for dijet production under the harmonic oscillator approximation for Wilson line averages—consistent with earlier findings for single-gluon production in p+A collisions; explicit NN-eikonal contributions are obtained; analytical results for the back-to-back limit are derived.
AI.conclusion: Finite longitudinal nuclear size induces non-eikonal corrections starting at NN-eikonal order for dijet DIS off nuclei within the harmonic oscillator model; the vanishing of NE corrections reinforces universality of this feature across different observables and collision systems, suggesting robustness of the underlying color-glass condensate framework beyond eikonal limits.

title: Evaluation of QED cross sections in strong magnetic fields
summary: Quantum electrodynamics (QED) becomes nonlinear when the magnetic field strength surpasses the critical Schwinger limit $B_Q \approx 4.41\cdot 10^{13}$ G. This limit is surpassed, for example, in the magnetospheres of a specific class of neutron stars known as magnetars, which has important consequences for magnetospheric plasma dynamics due to modifications in scattering cross sections. Using a formalism previously applied to the study of magnetic catalysis, I calculate the cross sections of all tree-level 1-to-2, 2-to-1, and 2-to-2 particle QED scattering processes that do not include a photon propagator. The calculations are done in a strong background magnetic field and the results are implemented into an open-source Python package. This article focuses on presenting the formalism and computational techniques required for the calculations, while the impact of the results on, e.g., magnetospheric plasma dynamics is discussed in a companion letter (Kiuru et al. 2026).

AI.tldr: This paper computes tree-level QED scattering cross sections (1→2, 2→1, 2→2) in ultra-strong magnetic fields (> Schwinger limit) relevant to magnetars, using a magnetic-catalysis-inspired formalism, and implements results in an open-source Python package.
AI.motivation: To quantify how nonlinear QED effects—arising when magnetic fields exceed the Schwinger critical field B_Q ≈ 4.41×10¹³ G—influence scattering processes in magnetar magnetospheres, where such fields occur and modify plasma dynamics.
AI.method: Adapts a formalism previously used for magnetic catalysis to compute all tree-level 1→2, 2→1, and 2→2 QED scattering amplitudes excluding photon propagators, in the presence of a static, uniform, strong background magnetic field; results are encoded in an open-source Python package.
AI.result: Analytic and numerically implementable expressions for the magnetic-field-dependent cross sections of the specified scattering processes; packaged as open-source Python code.
AI.conclusion: The developed formalism and computational framework enable accurate evaluation of nonlinear QED scattering in extreme magnetic fields; its astrophysical implications for magnetar plasma dynamics are deferred to a companion letter.
